title: Unpacking, enumerate, zip, and starred expressions
sources: Python documentation: built-in enumerate and zip functions
masterChecklist: Sequence operations, iterable protocol, unpacking, starred expressions, enumerate, zip, sorted and reversed
Collections, iteration, order preservation, unequal lengths and defensive data handling
Readable loop design, index/value pairing and explicit validation
whyItMatters: Data often arrives as pairs, rows, or ordered sequences. Unpacking names the parts clearly, enumerate gives an index without a manual counter, and zip joins parallel sequences—but zip can silently stop at the shorter input if you do not check lengths.
simpleExplanation: Unpacking assigns items from an iterable to several names. A starred target collects remaining items. enumerate yields an index and value. zip yields one tuple from each iterable at a time. These are concise tools, but a program must decide whether unequal inputs are valid before relying on zip.
mentalModel: Unpacking is opening a labeled lunch box and placing each item in its tray. enumerate writes row numbers while you read. zip is pairing socks from two baskets; when one basket runs out, ordinary zip stops, which may hide an unmatched sock.
outcomes: Use a starred name to capture a documented remainder.

realWorldExample.scenario: A study report combines lesson titles with minutes while displaying a numbered review list.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: If titles has three items and minutes has two, zip silently produces only two pairs. A report can therefore omit a lesson without an error.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Validate that parallel inputs have the same expected length, use enumerate for display indexes, and prefer a record/dictionary structure when fields naturally belong together.

workedExample.code:
titles = ['variables', 'loops', 'files']
minutes = [15, 20, 25]

if len(titles) != len(minutes):
    raise ValueError('titles and minutes must have the same length')

for number, (title, duration) in enumerate(zip(titles, minutes), start=1):
    print(f'{number}. {title}: {duration} minutes')

first, *later = titles
print(first, later)
explanation: The length check makes the parallel-data rule explicit before zip can truncate.
zip produces a title/minutes pair for each aligned position.
enumerate adds a display number starting at 1 without manually updating a counter.
first, *later unpacks the first title and collects the rest in a new list.
workedExample.expectedOutput:
1. variables: 15 minutes
2. loops: 20 minutes
3. files: 25 minutes
variables ['loops', 'files']
workedExample.safeExperiment: Remove one minutes value. Confirm that the explicit length check raises before an incomplete report is printed.

procedure: Describe whether sequence order and equal length are part of the data contract.
Unpack only after a sequence shape is known or controlled.
Use enumerate when an index is for display or position-aware logic.
Validate parallel iterable lengths when truncation would be a bug.
Use a list of records when each row's fields should travel together.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming zip raises when inputs have different lengths.
commonMistakes.why: Ordinary zip stops at the shortest iterable.
commonMistakes.avoid: Validate lengths or use a strict policy where appropriate for the Python version/project.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using an unpacking pattern with the wrong number of items.
commonMistakes.why: Python raises a ValueError when the sequence cannot match the assignment target.
commonMistakes.avoid: Validate the input shape or use a starred target when a variable-length remainder is expected.

commonMistakes.mistake: Maintaining a manual index while also using enumerate.
commonMistakes.why: Two counters can drift and obscure the loop's purpose.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use enumerate as the single source of the display index.

lab.title: Create a safe numbered study report
lab.safety: Uses only fictional lesson titles and local numeric durations.
lab.starterCode:
titles = ['variables', 'loops']
minutes = [15, 20]

# Validate lengths, then print numbered title/duration pairs.
guidedSteps: Unpack each pair into title and duration.
checks: Uses enumerate rather than a manual counter.
lab.solutionExplanation: The length check protects against zip silently dropping an unmatched value. The loop reads naturally because enumerate provides the display number while zip provides one aligned title/duration pair.
challenges: Predict the output when both lists have two items.
Find the bug: remove the length check and give minutes one fewer item.
Experiment: unpack first, *later from the titles list and explain what later contains.

projectConnection.milestone: Display a numbered aligned report only after validating its parallel input lists, then refactor to records if fields should remain attached.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: An unequal input list cannot silently omit a lesson from the report, and the loop has no manual index counter.

assessment.question: What does ordinary zip do with unequal-length iterables?
assessment.answer: It stops when the shortest iterable is exhausted.
assessment.explanation: That can silently omit unmatched values unless the contract is checked.

assessment.question: What does enumerate add to a loop?
assessment.answer: An index alongside each yielded value.
assessment.explanation: It avoids a separate manual counter.

assessment.question: What does a starred unpacking target collect?
assessment.answer: The remaining items that are not assigned to the other named targets.
assessment.explanation: It is useful when a variable-length remainder is part of the intended shape.
